svg.title: Epoch invalidation timeline and the G4A-01 interleaving
svg.desc: Two threads over time. A leader finalizes a fetch holding the shard mutex. An invalidation thread bumps the tenant epoch without taking the shard mutex. If the bump lands between the fence check and the epoch re-read, the old body is stamped with the new epoch. This was reproduced only with an injected yield point in a sandbox; the proposed fix is not integrated.
svg.text: Figure 4.4: Epoch invalidation, and the G4A-01 interleaving (NOT a normal run)
Status: reproduced ONLY with a yield point injected in a sandbox copy (debug build, one run). No natural-schedule hit in
3,160,958 fills over 20 s. Fix proposal exists in docs/research/g4a01_race/proposal.patch and is NOT integrated.
Normal ordering (invalidate before the fence check)
tenant acme at epoch 3. Fetch starts: entry epochs stamped (3, 0). Invalidation: acme epoch becomes 4, acknowledged.
finalize_fetch: state epochs (3, 0) differ from current (4, 0), so the body is not stored (stale_writes_prevented).
Waiters still get the old body, even those who joined after the bump (G4A-08, separate OPEN finding). Cache stays clean.
The race (invalidate lands between fence check and epoch re-read)
Leader thread: finalize_fetch
Invalidation thread
t0 begin_fetch: stamp entry epochs (3,0),
record op_gen. Origin returns body B1.
t1 lock shard mutex (held until the end)
fence check: (3,0) == current (3,0): PASS
window: shard mutex held, but the
invalidator never takes it. Work here:
eviction loop (up to 32), byte checks,
pending-freshness handling
t2 try_invalidate_tenant("acme")
tenant_epochs: 3 to 4; snapshot swapped;
returns 4 to the caller (acknowledged)
no ordering
t3 re-read epochs: now (4,0)
store B1, stamp entry epochs (4,0)
(new epoch on an old body)
t4 any later GET / begin_fetch:
entry (4,0) == current (4,0): HIT
serves B1 until its TTL ends
Proposed fix (sandbox only): stamp the epochs the fence check validated
At t1 remember (3,0). At t3 stamp (3,0) instead of re-reading. After t2 the entry then reads as epoch-stale: the next
read drops it. Sandbox result: 4 of 4 tests pass with the patch; 2 of 4 fail without it. Epoch changes need an independent
review and a failing-first test (CLAUDE.md section 5); neither is done. Reproduction shows possibility, not frequency.
